That is a distinction I would not have made. What is the difference in practice?
A prediction is a single answer. A forecast is a range, with the reasoning attached, so somebody can argue with it.
So when people ask you what is going to happen, what do you actually say?
I give them two scenarios and I say which one I would bet on. Then I say what would have to be true for me to be wrong.
By that standard I have never made a forecast in my life. I have only ever made predictions and defended them.

Three things on the year ahead, and then I will hand back to you. First, growth. Growth will probably have slowed by the middle of the year, and I want to be precise about that word probably, because I am not telling you it is certain. Second, the direction. The direction is inevitable at this point, in the sense that the momentum is already there and nobody in any government is going to reverse it. What is genuinely uncertain is the timing, and it may stay uncertain for another two years, which is an uncomfortable thing to say on the radio. And third, a piece of advice that costs you nothing. If somebody gives you a date and a number in the same sentence, stop listening. One of the two will be wrong, and it will take the other one down with it.

When somebody who has learned English makes a prediction, the tense is almost always right. What is missing is something else entirely. It is the degree of certainty. In Portuguese, and in most languages, the voice carries that: the same words said two different ways are two different claims, and everybody in the room hears the difference. English puts it in the words instead. So there are levels, and they are worth learning as a set. It could be, which is a possibility you are not betting on. It might well be, which is a strong possibility you would take seriously. And it will probably be, which is where you are willing to be quoted. Three degrees, three sets of words. And this matters much more abroad than it does at home, because a written sentence, or one said over a bad connection, keeps every word and loses every bit of the voice. Anything you were carrying in your tone alone arrives flattened.
